reasons: backend/internal/server/mcpoauth.go:106-110 (mcpResource) + :376 (mcpAudienceAccepted): when mcp.oauth.resource is empty and general publicUrl is empty, the resource identifier is built from requestOrigin() — i.e. r.Host / X-Forwarded-Host — and that value is then accepted as a valid aud. Reproduced end-to-end: enable MCP OAuth, clear general_config.publicUrl (settings_ui.go:270-283 allows this at any time with no cross-check), set trusted_proxy_cidrs=['192.0.2.0/24'], send POST /mcp with X-Forwarded-Host: other-releasedock.internal and a token whose aud is http://other-releasedock.internal/mcp and azp is NOT in mcp.oauth.audience -> 200 tools/list. validMCPOrigin (mcp.go:122) does not close this: it runs after withAuth and only checks r.Host, not X-Forwarded-Host. Fix: delete the requestOrigin fallback in mcpResource; when both mcp.oauth.resource and publicUrl are empty set Active=false with InactiveWhy (so /mcp returns the plain 401 and metadata returns 404). Add a test that fixes this: enable, clear publicUrl, set a trusted proxy, send X-Forwarded-Host + a token whose aud matches it, assert 401 and that the log says inactive/no resource identifier. Optionally also refuse clearing publicUrl in putGeneralSettings while mcp_oauth_enabled=TRUE and mcp_oauth_resource=''.

backend/internal/server/server.go:349 (withAuth, 'MCP OAuth token rejected'): the refusal log carries reason and ip but no request ID. The request ID middleware (server.go:477-481) only writes it to w.Header().Set("X-Request-ID", …) — it is not in ctx — so read w.Header().Get("X-Request-ID") in withAuth and add it as request_id to that Warn (and to the inactive path, which goes through the same Warn). Never pass an empty string. Then extend mcpoauth_test.go:532-534 (TestATokenIsRefusedForTheRightReason) so each bad-token case asserts the log line contains both the original check text (already done) AND request_id=<the X-Request-ID value from response.Header()> non-empty; same for the inactive case in TestMCPOAuthOffByDefaultChangesNothing:355.

backend/internal/server/mcpoauth.go:663-684 (mcpSigningKey): cache.mu is held across fetchMCPSigningKeys, which does OIDC discovery + the JWKS GET (up to 10s). One unknown kid blocks every concurrent token verification on the mutex, and a slow/dead Keycloak stalls all MCP auth. Also, when cache.keys==nil and the fetch fails, cache.fetched is never updated, so every following request re-fetches immediately (no mcpOAuthKeyRetry throttle) — a forged-kid stream hammers Keycloak. Fix: under the lock only read (keys, fetched, issuer) and decide; unlock; fetch with the request ctx; re-lock to store. Record the attempt time on failure too so a failed discovery is cached for mcpOAuthKeyRetry. Add a test with a fake IdP whose JWKS handler blocks/fails: (a) a valid-kid token verifies while an unknown-kid fetch is in flight, (b) a second unknown-kid request inside the retry window does not hit the IdP again.
notes: Verified OK: migration 025 is ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS only with mcp_oauth_enabled DEFAULT FALSE — additive, off by default, revertable. TestMCPOAuthOffByDefaultChangesNothing proves a fresh install behaves identically (metadata 404, no WWW-Authenticate, token refused with the same body as a bad key, personal key still works).

Ran the full new test set against a throwaway Postgres 16 (docker) with TEST_POSTGRES_DSN: 11/11 pass, plus existing MCP/OIDC/API-key tests pass. Tests are real end-to-end (handler chain, schema-isolated DB, fake IdP with real RSA/EC keys, buffer-captured slog) and each bad-token case asserts the original check text in the log and that the token itself is not logged.

Verified: no account is created or reactivated (users count asserted; active=TRUE in the lookup; username match restricted to auth_source='oidc'); ID tokens, cnf-bound tokens, HS256/none, wrong issuer, foreign key, expired, nbf all refused; empty scope intersection refuses (never unlimited); Principal.Has with ViaAPIKey and empty scopes = nothing; all three ViaAPIKey gates (rbac_policy.go:55, resources.go:399, server.go:413) apply to the SSO principal; tokens are only honoured on /mcp (REST 401 with no challenge); signature verified before payload is parsed; no secret in logs/responses/settings GET.

Only new unauthenticated routes are the RFC 9728 metadata documents; they 404 unless Active. Settings PUT validates all MCP keys before the single UPDATE (tested). No existing console setting keys were removed. Branch is directly on top of origin/main (no rebase needed). No out-of-scope changes.

The probe test used to reproduce the aud bypass was deleted after running; the worktree is clean. The reproduction steps are in reasons[0] so the next session can turn it into the permanent regression test.
